messages:
toni (Sales): Heads-up from RedwoodHealth procurement: OF redline wants DocuSign ID check for every signer AND a hard notarization clause for any contract > $200k. They also want a 99.9% SLA with sliding credits up to 25% monthly. This is a 3mo dedicated POC, estimated spend ~$38k. Need legal + eng take so I can push back.

samir (Legal): Please paste the exact procurement language if you have it. High-level: notarization at that threshold is unusual and problematic for quick POCs. We typically accept DocuSign ID verification but refuse notarization for <$250k unless special circumstances. SLA ask sounds high for a tiny isolated pool.

toni (Sales): Verbatim: "Provider must require DocuSign identity verification for all signatories. Provider shall provide 99.9% uptime; service credits accrue for each 0.1% below target up to 25% of monthly fees. Provider shall comply with Customer notarization requirements for contracts exceeding $200,000."

maya (Solutions): Technically we can enable ID Check in the DocuSign envelope. Dedicated POC pool can be provisioned in ~3 business days. But because it's single-tenant and short-lived, variance means committing 99.9% is risky.

own (Engineering): Agreed. Our Dedicated SLO offering in contracts is 99.5% for reserved pools. We should also be explicit about measurement windows (rolling 30-day) and exclusions (scheduled maintenance, customer network, force majeure). Otherwise credits can balloon.

samir (Legal): Proposed counter language to put in OF/MSA redline: 1) For Proof-of-Concept engagements, Provider offers a 99.5% uptime SLA. 2) Service credits for POCs are limited to the aggregate fees paid for the POC term. 3) Provider accepts electronic signatures executed via DocuSign; DocuSign identity verification satisfies Provider's signer authentication requirements. 4) Notarization requests for contracts under $250,000 are subject to escalation and are not a baseline requirement for POCs. Any objections?

linda (Finance): We can accept capping credits to POC fees. For negotiation levers, Finance can authorize a conversion credit: if Customer executes an annual Dedicated commitment within 60 days of POC completion, Provider will issue a one-time credit equal to 7.5% of the POC fees (example: ~$2,850 on $38k). Recommend we state dollar caps in the OF: credit cap = $38,000; conversion bonus = $2,850.

toni (Sales): Procurement will want dollar figures, so thank you for the example. I'll confirm the final POC total but plan to use those numbers as a starting point. Also they insisted PO number must appear on invoice and that the procurement approver + legal sign. I'll set DocuSign routing accordingly.

docusign-bot: DocuSign envelope template "Redwood POC OF" created (tpl_7744). Auth option: ID Check available. Template note: add optional Notary addendum for >$200k deals (manual escalate).

own (Engineering): I'll draft a short SLA carveout to attach to the redline clarifying: measurement (rolling 30-day window), exclusions (scheduled maintenance with 72h notice, acts of customer/third parties), and definition of "availability" (inference API vs control plane). Post in ticket.

samir (Legal): I'll prepare the redline reflecting the 99.5% POC SLA, credit caps, DocuSign clause, and the escalation path for notarization. Will upload to procurement ticket by EOD. If procurement insists on notarization for this $38k POC, we'll ask for written justification and route to exec approval.

toni (Sales): Plan: Samir uploads redline, Owen adds technical carveouts, Linda will lock the exact dollar caps once I confirm final invoice amount, and I'll prepare the DocuSign envelope with ID Check enabled. If procurement tries to force notarization, I'll escalate to Legal + Sales leadership. Thanks all :thumbsup:
